ResearchProjectDef.label: basic earthworks
ResearchProjectDef.description: Simple excavation and fill techniques. Colonists can dig soil for fill material and lay packed fill over poor ground. Moving dirt is hard work — expect long job times and dirty colonists.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->dug irrigation canals on a dustworld
subject_story->reclaimed flooded farmland after a monsoon season

ResearchProjectDef.label: composting
ResearchProjectDef.description: Turn plant matter and hay into compost. Compost can be worked into soil to create artificial rich soil — powerful, but it will slowly degrade without maintenance or a soil stabilizer.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->ran a community compost yard on an agriworld

ResearchProjectDef.label: field tillage
ResearchProjectDef.description: Till existing soil into a temporary high-fertility seedbed. Tilled soil is excellent for a few seasons, then collapses back — sometimes into packed, exhausted ground if overused.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->taught contour ploughing to frontier farmers

ResearchProjectDef.label: drainage works
ResearchProjectDef.description: Drain marshy soil and fill shallow water with engineered embankments. Extremely labour-intensive. Draining large areas raises geological stress and may invite flooding backlash.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->directed a marsh reclamation project that nearly bankrupted a colony

ResearchProjectDef.label: soil engineering
ResearchProjectDef.description: Industrial soil science: build soil stabilizers that maintain artificial soils in a radius and bleed off geological stress. Without them, large terraformed farms will rot back into gravel and mud.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->stabilized dunes that once buried a coastal city

ResearchProjectDef.label: hydro-terraforming
ResearchProjectDef.description: Advanced water management: reclaim chest-deep water and reinforce reclaimed banks. Still cannot conquer ocean deeps. High material cost and significant geological risk.

rulesStrings.li: subject_story->redirected a river that drowned three outposts before it held
